intro: NMIMS Hyderabad and NALSAR both sit in Hyderabad, and this page compares their recorded Integrated Law fees, placements, admission routes and campus setting, using our database and official pages we opened in 2026.

NMIMS Hyderabad vs NALSAR is not a single winner. NMIMS Hyderabad is recorded as a private institute, while NALSAR is public. NALSAR holds a NIRF 2025 rank of 3; NMIMS Hyderabad has no NIRF rank on this page.

sections.heading: NMIMS Hyderabad vs NALSAR for Integrated Law: which is better in 2026
paragraphs: Choose NALSAR if you want a public Integrated Law option and the admission route and fees that usually come with a government or state university campus.
Choose NMIMS Hyderabad if a private campus, its specific specialisation or its recorded placement year fits your plan better, after you have checked the official fee notice.
NMIMS Hyderabad lists BA.LLB (HONS), BBA LLB (Hons). NALSAR lists BA.LLB (HONS).

sections.heading: Fees: what our records show, and what the official pages say
paragraphs: On this page we quote a programme total when we hold a Total Fees record, and we skip application, hostel-only or short-course rows so a registration fee is not treated as tuition.
Our records list ₹1.25 lakh a year as tuition fees for NMIMS Hyderabad's BA.LLB (HONS). Treat that as a year figure, not a confirmed full-programme total, until you check the official notice.

NALSAR's official 2026–27 fee circular for the first year of B.A., LL.B. (Hons.) lists tuition of ₹1.65 lakh and a first-year total of ₹3.17 lakh for general candidates (₹3.11 lakh for SC/ST), including user charges, mess advance, one-time payments and refundable deposits. Tuition rises by ₹5,000 in each later year.
If fees are your only filter, confirm the current official circular for the exact programme and batch you will join, because year figures and older rows can understate the real cost.

sections.heading: Placements compared
paragraphs: Our records do not show a 2020 or later flagship placement year for NMIMS Hyderabad on this page. Ask the institute for its latest official placement report for the same programme.
In our records, NALSAR's 2023 figures are an average of ₹16 lakh and a highest of ₹40 lakh for BA.LLB (HONS). These are historical batch outcomes, not a salary promise.
If you are comparing offers, use the latest official placement report from each institute and match the programme name, not an executive or certificate batch.

sections.heading: Admission and eligibility
paragraphs: NMIMS Hyderabad admits to its five-year integrated law programmes through CLAT, as set out in the NMIMS 2026 admission handout. Confirm the current handout before you apply.
NALSAR's B.A., LL.B. (Hons.) shortlist is through CLAT, followed by the university's fee and document formalities after a seat is allotted.
Eligibility wording can change by cycle. Use the current official admission brochure rather than last year's cut-off stories.

sections.heading: Location and campus
paragraphs: Both campuses are in Hyderabad, Telangana. The choice is less about moving city and more about the programme, fees and admission route.
Visit both campuses if you can, or at least read the official hostel and location notes, before you accept an offer.

sections.heading: Verdict: who should pick which college
paragraphs: If you want a national-law-university BA LL.B. through CLAT and the NIRF 2025 Law rank 3 campus in this pair, NALSAR is the stronger academic fit.

If you specifically want a private NMIMS Hyderabad integrated law seat, still plan for CLAT, and confirm the official year-wise fee, which is recorded here as ₹1.25 lakh a year in tuition and may not be the full five-year cost.
